Assuming:
- GitHub repo owner/org is "acme" and the GitHub account/login is "marcus".
- AWS IAM user name is "marcus" and the IAM group is "prod-deployers".
- You have admin credentials for GitHub (gh CLI) and AWS CLI. Adjust --profile or environment variables as needed.

Exact commands to run:

1) Remove Marcus as a GitHub collaborator (write access) from the repo
- Remove:
  gh api -X DELETE /repos/acme/billing-service/collaborators/marcus
- Verify (expected 404 if no longer a collaborator):
  gh api -I /repos/acme/billing-service/collaborators/marcus

(If Marcus was granted via a team instead of as a collaborator, replace with the appropriate team removal:
  gh api -X DELETE /orgs/acme/teams/<team-slug>/memberships/marcus
)

2) Remove Marcus from the AWS IAM group "prod-deployers"
- Remove:
  aws iam remove-user-from-group --group-name prod-deployers --user-name marcus
  (add --profile <profile> if you use named profiles)
- Verify (should return no matching user entry):
  aws iam get-group --group-name prod-deployers --query "Users[?UserName=='marcus']" --output text

Optional verification steps you may run after the above:
- List Marcus' repo permissions (GitHub):
  gh api /repos/acme/billing-service/collaborators/marcus --silent || echo "not a collaborator"
- Check Marcus' IAM groups (AWS):
  aws iam list-groups-for-user --user-name marcus

One-line audit note for the ticket:
Removed GitHub write access to acme/billing-service and removed user "marcus" from AWS IAM group "prod-deployers" per legal-approved offboarding, effective today.

If any of the assumptions above differ (e.g., repo access granted via a GitHub team, different GitHub username, or a different AWS username/profile), tell me and I’ll provide the exact adjusted commands.
